name: ow_nav_downstairs
doc: Stands in for saves/ow_w0.state.chk, the checkpoint ct.exe --navworld saved 45 frames after it walked Crono down from his bedroom (loc 002 -> 001) on the way to the original overworld capture; the downstairs objects equal it byte for byte. Two things of the bedroom outlive the load and are matched: Crono WALKS (no B) down-right into the staircase, so the bedroom's obj1 walk animation is left at $1600 = 03 07 / $1680 = 01 03 (both survive into the overworld's dead object blocks); and he reaches the stairs on the reference's play clock ($0400-$0403), because the location load seeds the RNG cursor $01F8 from its frame byte (C0/0C70 `LDA $0400 / STA $F8`) and the downstairs cat (obj9) wanders on that cursor. Not matched (70 bytes), none of them read downstairs: $0108 (the exit's tile, 0F against 0E), objects 16-19's leftover $1001 bytes, a $0500 table and four OAM rows (+3 / +5), stack garbage and the sprite-frame buffers $7F:3AC6-3BFF.
